parsedVerdict.reasoning: Both files deal with loans, so the concern itself holds together. The module is still not one coherent unit, for three reasons. First, the two services reach persistence in different ways. LendingService goes through gateway abstractions (BookGateway, MemberGateway, LoanGateway), maps records into domain models and raises LendingError. LoanHistoryService queries Prisma directly through an injected PrismaService and returns raw rows mapped into a local LoanEvent interface. Second, LoanHistoryService bypasses its own injected dependency: note() creates a new PrismaClient() instead of using this.db, which eventsOf() does use. Third, both services generate IDs the same way, with an in-memory counter on the instance (sequence → `loan-N`, counter → `evt-N`). That ID rule is written twice instead of living in one place.

violations.message: note() creates `new PrismaClient()` instead of using the injected `db: PrismaService`, so it skips its own injected dependency. eventsOf() uses this.db, so the class reaches the database in two different ways.
Uses PrismaService/PrismaClient directly instead of a gateway. That doesn't match the module's gateway pattern used in LendingService (BookGateway, LoanGateway, MemberGateway).
The in-memory ID rule (`private sequence` → `loan-N`) is the same one LoanHistoryService writes again (`private counter` → `evt-N`). This rule should live in one place.
